Title: Nurse Martha Muthoni Stays True to Purpose
NewsSummary: The SONAM EA graduand shares why nursing is a rewarding career
NewsContent:
For Martha Muthoni, the path to earning her Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Post-RN BScN) at Aga Khan University (AKU) was not an easy one. With over a decade of experience as a registered nurse in both private and government hospitals, Martha was already established in her career when she decided to take the leap and pursue a degree that would expand her knowledge, sharpen her skills, and propel her into the next phase of her professional journey.

Martha currently works in the Accident and Emergency Department at Kenyatta International Hospital, where she first felt the call to pursue further education. "My passion for nursing and healthcare really ignited in the emergency department," Martha explains. It was here that she realized the importance of not only improving patient care but also refining her own capabilities as a nurse.

Her journey at AKU was transformative. She fondly credits the university's scholarship programme, faculty support, and extensive resources as the key factors that enabled her to thrive in her studies. "Receiving a scholarship made everything so much easier," Martha says. "It lifted the financial burden and allowed me to focus fully on my academic and personal growth. It was an opportunity I'm extremely grateful for."

But Martha's experience was more than just academic success. One of the most profound moments during her studies was a trip to Tanzania, where she had the chance to meet with healthcare leaders. "That trip was a revelation," she reflects. "It opened my eyes to the broader role nurses can play in Africa's healthcare system, and it inspired me to mentor and precept young nurses. It's something I've become deeply passionate about."

Balancing the demands of work, family, and school was no small feat. Martha, however, credits her strict time management and intentionality as the cornerstones of her success. "It was challenging," she admits. "But I learned how to allocate specific times for studying, family, and work. It wasn't easy, but it kept me grounded."

The emotional resilience required to navigate such a rigorous academic journey was another key lesson she took away from AKU. "AKU taught me resilience," she says. "It was a tough journey, but it was worth every moment."

One of the aspects of AKU that Martha holds dear is the open-door policy of its faculty. "Whenever I needed help, the professors were always there for me. That kind of support made all the difference in managing academic stress and anxiety," she shares.

Martha also highlights her clinical rotations and certain classes as particularly memorable. "English writing helped me improve my communication skills as a nurse. Anatomy was another favourite-Dr Beda Olabu made the subject come alive in such a memorable way."

Her degree has not only expanded her knowledge of medical conditions but also given her the tools to address gaps in nursing practices. Looking ahead, Martha's aspirations are big. "My long-term goal is to open my own practice focused on newborn care and home-based services for mothers," she says. This vision, she explains, stems from a passion for a space in healthcare that is often overlooked.

Martha's journey doesn't end here. She plans to pursue further certifications, a master's degree, and ultimately a PhD. "AKU has taught me the value of continuous learning, and I know I have a lot more to accomplish," she reflects.

Her advice to future nurses? "Nursing is a calling," she says with conviction. "It's emotionally and physically demanding, but it's so rewarding if you stay true to your purpose and always remember the bigger picture."

As Martha prepares for Convocation, she reflects on her journey with a sense of pride and anticipation. "It's been a long road, but I'm finally here. I can't wait to wear my gown and celebrate with my family. It's been an unforgettable experience, and it's just the beginning."
